core.title: The Station Master's route map keeps direct train routes when interlocking routes are added
core.given: The Station Master (the composition root) has a route map with at least one interlocking route object - an entry that carries an interlocking reference and the location of its definition instead of naming the train directly
core.when: you add or change route-map entries or their dispatch in the composition root
core.then: The route map MUST accept both a direct train reference and an interlocking route object, and existing direct mappings MUST stay valid.
prefer: A mixed route map: direct actions map straight to their train reference, while interlocked actions map to an interlocking route object (interlocking reference plus the location of its definition)
avoid: Converting, removing or rejecting existing direct train mappings when you add interlocking routes
unless: The route map declares no interlocking route object: a Station Master with only direct routes carries no interlocking obligation
core.why: The interlocking route is additive, so the existing direct mapping remains valid. The train executor executes the train in both cases; the runner-delegation part of this convention enforces that.
evidence: The route map and its dispatch accept both direct train references and interlocking route objects
Existing direct mappings still resolve to their trains. Direct entries do not have to be present: an interlocking-only map is acceptable
verification: Source statement (normative MUST): the Station Master MUST support both direct and interlocking-enabled routing, and the route map MUST admit a direct train reference AND an interlocking route object. This requires support for both forms, not that both kinds of entry be present.

The automated findings for the sibling parts of this convention (unlinked interlocking, missing train delegation) do not cover this part; check it by reviewing the route-map declaration and its dispatch. Which construct is inspected and how the route forms are recognized is the per-stack checker's concern.
Scope: the composition root only (local name and path from the profile); nothing outside that role fires.

values: the composition root's route map contains at least one interlocking route object

fires: A task adds an interlocking route to a route map that already has direct entries
A task adds the first interlocking route to a route map that has no direct entries
An agent edits route-map handling in a composition root that already holds interlocking routes
doesNotFire: The route map holds only direct train references
Files that do not play the composition-root role

neutralityNotes: ATDD vocabulary (Station Master, train, interlocking, route map) is treated as framework-neutral, per the neutral rule id coder.station-master.interlocking-routing-route-forms; the stack's local names and shapes come from the profile (roles.composition_root.name/path, urn.train, idiom.routing#route_map). The concrete route-map construct (JOURNEY_MAP, {interlockingId, path}, the mixed-map example) has no neutral wording and is carried by the proposed idiom.routing#route_map key plus the Bun reference example in bun.json. TrainRunner/InterlockingRunner are named only at role level (train executor, interlocking resolver) because the call model itself is the sibling runner-delegation part. Stack applicability gating (typescript/javascript, the atdd.workspace.bun workspace note, and the 'Non-Bun stacks' doesNotFire entry) is per-realization and stays bunOnly; the neutral doesNotFire covers it as 'files that do not play the composition-root role'.
